A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FOLDER and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-C. Material can be matched across layout changes, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLLM benchmark evaluations, training and inference measurements, and empirical ablations in Tables 1-12 and Figures 2-4 and 6-9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, efficiency and ablation results, including those in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same iterative FOLD procedure, late-block token reduction, matching and aggregation operations. The implementation and simplified variant in the appendices are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet-1k analyses, COCO captioning task and image/video multimodal benchmarks. No dataset, domain or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: pooling, FastV and Turbo in Table 1; Turbo in Tables 2, 3 and 5; and FastV/Turbo in Table 6. The corresponding original-model comparisons and appendix variants also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, reduction ratios, pretraining/SFT procedure and evaluation choices remain identical. Both retain exact matching versus LLM evaluation, first-token timing, and the batch-size-40 memory measurement protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the same propagation-effect, merging-position, aggregation, matching-function and simplified-FOLDER analyses in Figures 2-4 and 6-9 and Tables 7-12. Moving Table 8 does not add or remove an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars for these experiments. Statistical and uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-12 and the plotted findings retain the same results. For example, Table 1 retains FOLDER averages of 54.8/56.1 for 7B/13B at 66% reduction, and Table 4 retains 61.2 with 66% reduction during both training and inference.

T1.justification: The SVD-based energy definition and bound argument, EMD formulation, aggregation equations and appendix matching-function formula are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: information-guided visual token reduction and a plug-and-play module that accelerates training and inference while maintaining or improving performance.

C2.justification: The propagation, noise-smoothing and regularization interpretations are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same limitations concerning exact-match evaluation, the unclear performance-boost mechanism and the need for further theoretical explanation.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same insertion location, token-size bookkeeping, matching parameter alpha=5, simplified implementation and training details. Hardware descriptions and code-release/access information are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 89 references and positioning relative to ToMe, Turbo, FastV and concurrent work. Changed citation-page backreferences reflect pagination rather than added or removed research.

P1.justification: v2 adds Shuai Xiao to the author list and updates the version/date header. Scientific prose, terminology and section ordering remain unchanged apart from text reflow.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 3 to page 4, Figure 4 shifts within page 4, and Table 8 moves from page 8 to page 9. Spacing and text placement change, while figure contents, table structures and captions remain unchanged; appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v2 changes the author list and modestly adjusts layout while retaining the same scientific explanation, results, reproducibility information and limitations. These presentation changes establish no meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
